content.text: {"primary_meaning": "Abundance, prosperity, and the richness of God's blessing. In most Christian teaching and commentary, butter/curds (Hebrew chemah) functions as an emblem of plenty — the fatness of the land and the overflow of divine provision — since curdled milk was a staple luxury of pastoral abundance in the ancient Near East.", "primary_basis": ["Job 29:6 (Job's former prosperity: 'when my steps were washed with butter')", "Deuteronomy 32:14 ('butter of kine, and milk of sheep' among the blessings God gave Israel)", "Job 20:17 ('brooks of honey and butter' as the abundance the wicked will not enjoy)", "Isaiah 7:15, 21-22 ('butter and honey shall he eat' in the Immanuel prophecy)", "Genesis 18:8 (Abraham sets butter, milk, and a calf before his heavenly visitors — generous hospitality)", "2 Samuel 17:29 (provisions of butter brought to David — sustenance and provision)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Scarcity/remnant survival food: in Isaiah 7:15-22 many modern commentators read curds and honey not as luxury but as the diet of a depopulated, devastated land — food available when agriculture has collapsed and only livestock foraging remains — so the sign carries a note of judgment as well as survival.", "basis": ["Isaiah 7:15", "Isaiah 7:21-22"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Christological sign of the true humanity of Christ: patristic and later devotional writers (e.g., Irenaeus and subsequent commentators on the Immanuel prophecy) took 'butter and honey shall he eat' as evidence that the promised child would be genuinely human, eating ordinary infant food, and growing in moral discernment.", "basis": ["Isaiah 7:14-15"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Flattery, smooth deceit, and hypocrisy: words 'smoother than butter' while war is in the heart — butter as an image of treacherous, ingratiating speech.", "basis": ["Psalm 55:21", "Judges 5:25 (Jael's butter offered to Sisera before killing him is sometimes read as deceptive hospitality)"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Strife produced by pressing/provocation: the churning of milk bringing forth butter as a proverb that forcing/agitation produces conflict.", "basis": ["Proverbs 30:33"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Hospitality and generous welcome: butter as the best of the household set before guests.", "basis": ["Genesis 18:8", "Judges 5:25"], "prominence": "minority"}], "has_settled_consensus": false, "confidence": "medium", "notes": "Butter/curds (chemah) does not have a single, tightly settled symbolic meaning in Christian interpretation comparable to terms like 'leaven' or 'lamb.' The broadest and most frequently invoked association is abundance/rich provision, but the term's symbolic force is heavily context-dependent, and the most theologically discussed passage (Isaiah 7:15) is itself contested between 'abundance' and 'devastation-era subsistence' readings, with an additional patristic Christological layer. Translations vary between 'butter' (KJV) and 'curds' (most modern versions), which affects how commentators frame the image. Any author claiming one exclusive symbolic meaning would be going beyond recognizable consensus."}
